goals.h1: Peptides for hair loss, compared with the proven options.
goals.description: Peptides for hair loss next to finasteride and minoxidil: FDA status, evidence in people and price per month for each option, checked and dated.
goals.short_answer: Finasteride and minoxidil are the only treatments on this page the FDA has approved for hair loss, and generic finasteride starts at about $10 a month. Copper peptide serums are cosmetics: the evidence is from lab and follicle-culture studies, not from large trials in people. Injectable peptides sold for hair are not approved for any use, and we found no human evidence for hair.

goals.label: Hair
goals.intro: Finasteride and minoxidil are the only FDA-approved options. Copper peptide serums are cosmetics; injectable peptides sold for hair are not approved for any use.

goals.name: Skin
goals.label: Skin
goals.intro: Peptide creams and serums are cosmetics: legal to sell without approval, and judged on their own studies, which are small. The proven prescription option for wrinkles is tretinoin.

goals.name: Weight loss
goals.label: Weight loss
goals.intro: Two peptide drugs are FDA approved for weight management and need a prescription. Compounded copies and newer molecules sold online are not approved.

goals.name: Muscle and hormones
goals.label: Muscle and hormones
goals.intro: No peptide is FDA approved for building muscle. Tesamorelin is approved for one specific use in people with HIV; growth hormone peptides sold for muscle are not approved.
